newsitem.title: LEBANON: Five Red Army suspects indicted in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Five Red Army suspects indicted in Lebanon.

text.p: A Beirut investigative judge on Thursday issued an indictment charging five Japanese Red Army guerrillas with offences carrying up to 10 years in prison, judicial sources said.

In his indictment, issued after nearly one month of interrogations, judge Saeed Mirza said the charges included "passport forgery, illegal entry to Lebanon, and official stamps forgery", the sources said.
According to Lebanon's judicial system, a three-member judicial board needs to approve the indictment before suspects are sent to court.
Kazua Tohira, Haruo Wako, Mariko Yamamoto, Masao Adachi and Kozo Okamoto were arrested on February 15 in Beirut and Lebanon announced that it would try them in Lebanon.

A Lebanese woman, Umayya Abboud, arrested in connection with the case, would be tried for illegally practising medicine. She was found innocent of charges of collaboration in forgery offences, the sources said.
Japan had hoped to extradite the suspects to face international charges arising from guerrilla activity.
Lebanon and Japan do not have an extradition agreement.
Okamoto was involved in the May 1972 shootout at Tel Aviv's Lod airport in which 24 people died and 100 were wounded.
He was captured by Israeli forces and sentenced to life imprisonment but was released in a Palestinian-Israeli prisoner swap in May, 1985.

The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions. The Bekaa Valley was a haven during Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war for guerrilla groups including Lebanese Moslems and Marxists, Palestinians, Kurds and the Red Army.
